transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-20 14:00 PT
Duration: 50 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jasmin Patel (Peregrine - Head of ML), Omar Haddad (Peregrine - Platform), Lea Kim (Peregrine - Product)

Summary (auto): Quick triage of recent drop in extraction accuracy for 'delivery-window' slots; discussion of next steps for prompt curation, scoring thresholds, and guardrail rules. Action items assigned.

---Transcript---
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we are at the top of the hour. Quick check, audio ok?
[00:07] Jasmin: Yeah, sounds good. Sorry running a bit late, had a deck review.
[00:11] Marco: No worries. I pulled the latest evals you shared, Jasmin, and I can see the spike in false positives around the 3/27 batch.
[00:20] Jasmin: Yep, that one. We started seeing the extraction model mis-assign the delivery-window if the order comment contained time ranges like "after 6" or "evening" — it sometimes picks up the wrong timezone string.
[00:34] Omar: To add, we saw throughput dip on peak hours last week; not sure if that's related to batching config or the model taking longer on certain prompts.
[00:42] Lea: From product, this impacts the UI confirmation flow and causes more manual ops. We need a low false positive threshold.
[00:50] Avery: Good context. Two threads today: diagnose the regression signal in the scorecard, and iterate guardrails to reduce false positives. Marco, can you summarize the eval breakdown?
[01:00] Marco: Sure. So I ran the scorecard across 2k prompts — the overall A1 accuracy dropped from 92% to 86% on the weekly snapshot. The interesting part is precision for the 'window' slot fell to 78% while recall stayed 90% — so it's making more confident but wrong picks. Could be a prompt reweighting issue or a model variant change during the rollout.
[01:24] Jasmin: Hmm, we didn't change prompts from our side. There was a minor prompt template tweak in staging, though, around punctuation. Might be that.
[01:32] Marco: Also worth flagging tokenizer boundary quirks with quantized variants — we saw similar behavior when we switched to the 4-bit variant for cost reasons.
[01:42] Omar: That's the tradeoff we've been worried about: cost savings vs subtle accuracy hits. We run this at scale so unit cost matters.
[01:48] Avery: Understood. For POC success we agreed on >=90% precision for critical slots. Right now we're below that. Proposed plan: Jasmin to provide 500 edge-case prompts, Avery to share updated scoring spreadsheet, Marco to run a focused run on a dedicated pool and reproduce the regressions.
[02:05] Lea: Timeline? We need to unblock the UI fix by end of next week.
[02:09] Marco: I can prioritize the latency and accuracy sweep on a 4xA100 dedicated pool, should have preliminary numbers by Friday.
[02:18] Jasmin: I can get the edge prompts together by Thursday.
[02:23] Avery: Great. A couple guardrail ideas: 1) add a post-processing rule that ignores candidate windows under certain confidence or pattern matches, 2) require dual-model agreement for slot population on ambiguous prompts, 3) tighten the scorecard's precision threshold to 0.9 for the 'delivery-window' slot so we can trigger manual review faster.
[02:42] Omar: Dual-model agreement sounds expensive but acceptable as an on-fail fallback. How does Redwood recommend implementing that?
[02:50] Marco: We can do a quick route where the primary model runs normally, and only if the confidence is between 0.45-0.75 we call a smaller but higher-precision variant as a tie-breaker. That adds latency for only ~6% of requests.
[03:07] Jasmin: Does that play nicely with KV caching? We rely on prefix cache for templated prompts.
[03:12] Marco: Yes, the runtime will still leverage KV for the main path. The tie-breaker call can use cached keys if the prompt prefix matches; worst case we pay single-call latency overhead.
[03:20] Avery: Another compliance point raised by the customer last week: VPC deployment + KMS for keys. Jasmin, are you leaning private for the pilot?
[03:28] Jasmin: We prefer VPC but if dedicated hosted with SOC2 and audit logs is easier to spin up for the POC we can do that temporarily. Security is non-negotiable though.
[03:38] Marco: We have a private deployment option and a dedicated hosted option. For immediate benchmarking, dedicated hosted is faster to provision; private requires network setup but supports customer KMS and SAML SSO.
[03:51] Lea: Also, can we get per-token cost estimates if we enable the dual-model tie-breaker?
[03:57] Avery: We'll compute incremental cost — Marco, can you model cost with 6% tie-breaker calls?
[04:03] Marco: Yep, I'll include that in the benchmark sheet. Expect ~5-12% increase depending on sequence length.
[04:09] Jasmin: Back to the regression — any quick root causes? Maybe the prompt template punctuation tweak as I mentioned.
[04:16] Marco: There's a couple hypotheses: tokenizer boundary shifts with quantization, prompt template change, or a small model patch that altered beam scoring. We should do an A/B between the variant used on 3/20 and current.
[04:29] Omar: Can Redwood pin model versions for the duration of the POC? We're trying to limit variables.
[04:34] Avery: Absolutely, we can pin model versions and also enable controlled rollouts. We'll pin to the version you were on the week prior to the regression and run comparisons.
[04:41] Lea: Good. For the scorecard, can we get a breakdown by intent and slot so product can triage UI impact?
[04:49] Marco: I'll add per-intent/slot breakdown and a confusion matrix into the spreadsheet.
[04:55] Jasmin: On false positives, guardrail tweaks: can we add pattern heuristics? e.g., if the prompt contains timezone abbreviations like PST/EST then prefer timezone extraction, otherwise default to local-window.
[05:06] Marco: Yes, simple regex heuristics are cheap and effective. We'll add that as a first-pass filter before calling the model.
[05:14] Avery: Great. Also want to call out logging: we need more granular traces to find which prompts hit the fallback path. We'll enable token-level tracing for a sample subset — Marco will collect and redact before sharing.
[05:27] Omar: Make sure PII is redacted; we have strict audit rules.
[05:30] Marco: Agreed. We'll run the redaction pipeline before dropping logs into the shared drive.
[05:36] Lea: Quick question — any competitor differences we should be aware of? Jasmin asked about Anthropic earlier; how do we compare?
[05:43] Avery: Anthropic has strong safety primitives but less flexible deployment options for private KMS. OpenAI has broad model coverage but pricing and observability differ. Our differentiator here is being able to iterate guardrails and pin versions while giving you telemetry for scoring.
[06:00] Jasmin: Ok that helps.
[06:03] Avery: Next steps recap: Avery to send updated scoring spreadsheet + annotation guidelines; Marco to run latency/accuracy sweeps on dedicated pool and cost delta for tie-breaker; Jasmin to deliver 500 edge prompts. We'll reconvene Friday if preliminary numbers look off, otherwise Monday sync.
[06:21] Lea: Sounds good. Also can we get a short doc on how to enable the dual-model fallback in config?
[06:27] Marco: I'll add a stub playbook and config snippet to the shared drive (link: https://redwood.example.com/peregrine-playbooks).
[06:35] Jasmin: Thank you. One last thing — can you also include the SOC2 + VPC checklist? Our infosec will want that before we go dedicated.
[06:43] Avery: Will do, sending SOC2 artifacts and VPC setup checklist after the call.
[06:48] Omar: Thanks everyone.
[06:50] Avery: Thanks, we'll follow up with artifacts. Meeting adjourned.
